tono: cálido y festivo; cempasúchil, ofrenda, papel picado

arte.universo: Mexico across time, always in early November or at night: the Mexica city of Tenochtitlan with temple silhouettes, canals and copal smoke; a 16th-century colonial stone church in New Spain; and present-day Mexican homes and candlelit cemeteries full of orange cempasúchil marigolds, candles, colorful papel picado, pan de muerto and decorated sugar skulls. Warm, festive and respectful: no horror skeletons, no blood, nothing scary or graphic.

escena.accion: At night in a humble Mexican home, the Pasita stands before a home altar (ofrenda) with several levels covered in orange cempasúchil marigolds, lit candles, pan de muerto, fruit, small sugar skulls and framed photos seen only as soft blurred glowing rectangles; a path of marigold petals runs from the open front door to the altar
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-middle, seen from behind, backpack on, looking up at the ofrenda with wonder
escena.objeto: The ofrenda glowing with candles and marigolds; photo frames blurred with no faces visible
escena.foreground: Orange marigold petals on the tiled floor, slightly blurred
escena.background: Colorful papel picado with only abstract cut-out patterns (no letters) hanging across a dark room, the open door to the night street
escena.iluminacion: Warm golden candlelight against a deep dark room
escena.emocion: Warm waiting, tenderness, a festive night
escena.composicion: Medium-wide shot; the upper 42% dark ceiling with faint papel picado in shadow, calm for the title

escena.accion: At dusk on a stone plaza in Tenochtitlan, anonymous Mexica people seen from behind and far away carry baskets of maize, flowers and small breads toward a temple, with copal smoke rising from clay braziers
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-right, seen from behind, backpack on, watching the procession quietly
escena.objeto: Clay braziers with copal smoke and baskets of offerings: maize, flowers, small round breads
escena.foreground: A clay brazier with glowing embers and smoke, slightly blurred
escena.midground: The Pasita on the stone plaza
escena.background: Silhouette of a stepped temple pyramid and canals in the haze
escena.iluminacion: Deep blue dusk with warm orange glow from the braziers
escena.composicion: Wide shot; the upper 42% dark blue dusk sky with copal smoke

cuerpo: Un perro **xoloitzcuintle** guiaba a las almas.

escena.accion: On a misty path at night beside a calm dark river, a hairless dark-grey xoloitzcuintle dog walks ahead while the Pasita follows it, holding a small candle
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-left, three-quarter view from behind, backpack on, following the dog
escena.objeto: A friendly hairless xoloitzcuintle dog looking back toward the Pasita
escena.foreground: Smooth river stones and a few orange flowers, slightly blurred
escena.midground: The Pasita and the dog on the path
escena.background: Mist over the dark river and silhouettes of distant mountains
escena.iluminacion: Soft moonlight and the small warm candle
escena.emocion: Mystery and gentle companionship, not scary
escena.composicion: Wide shot; the upper 42% dark misty night sky

escena.accion: Inside a simple 16th-century colonial stone church in New Spain, rows of candles burn on the floor and a wooden table; anonymous people far away kneel in quiet prayer, seen from behind
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-middle, seen from behind, backpack on, standing in the aisle
escena.objeto: Many small candles and a few marigolds on the stone floor
escena.foreground: Candles on the floor, slightly blurred
escena.background: Thick stone arches and a high small window, people far away in the shadows
escena.iluminacion: Warm candlelight and a pale beam of light from the high window
escena.composicion: Medium-wide shot; the upper 42% dark stone vaults

cuerpo: Pan de muerto, velas, **copal y cempasúchil**.
Su color y su aroma **guían el camino**.

escena.accion: At dawn, the Pasita walks through a huge field of bright orange cempasúchil marigolds, carrying a small bundle of flowers in her arms
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-left, seen from behind, backpack on, flowers in her arms
escena.objeto: An endless field of orange marigolds
escena.foreground: Marigold blossoms very close to the camera, slightly blurred
escena.background: Distant volcano silhouette and anonymous farmers far away from behind
escena.iluminacion: Soft early sunlight, intense orange on the flowers
escena.composicion: Wide shot; the upper 42% dark blue pre-dawn sky

escena.accion: A Mexican cemetery at night glowing with hundreds of candles and marigolds on the graves; anonymous families sit together far away, seen from behind, sharing food and talking calmly
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-right, sitting on a low stone wall seen from behind, backpack beside her, watching the candlelight
escena.objeto: Graves covered with marigold arches and candles; simple crosses with no names or letters
escena.foreground: A row of candles and petals, slightly blurred
escena.background: A sea of candlelight and a small church silhouette
escena.iluminacion: Hundreds of warm candles against the dark night
escena.composicion: Wide shot; the upper 42% dark starry night sky

post:
1 y 2 de noviembre: Día de Muertos. 🧡🕯️

Mucho antes de la llegada de los españoles, los mexicas ya honraban a sus muertos con dos fiestas, el Miccailhuitontli y el Huey Miccailhuitl, que caían cerca de agosto. Creían que las almas viajaban al Mictlán, y que un perro xoloitzcuintle las acompañaba.

En el siglo XVI llegaron de España el Día de Todos Santos (1 de noviembre) y el de Fieles Difuntos (2 de noviembre). Las dos tradiciones se mezclaron: pan de muerto, velas, copal y cempasúchil, que en náhuatl quiere decir "veinte flores".

En 2008 la UNESCO inscribió las fiestas indígenas dedicadas a los muertos en su Lista del Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial de la Humanidad (ya las había proclamado obra maestra en 2003).

¿Qué no puede faltar en tu ofrenda? 👇
